definitions.explanation: A large, tall cloud formation that develops vertically, often associated with summer weather and thunderstorms. Named for its resemblance to a bald monk's head.

examples.japanese: ⟦{夏|なつ}→夏：02236_natsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{空|そら}→空：02216_sora⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{入道雲|にゅうどうぐも}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{見|み}える→見える：01165_mieru⟧。
examples.english: Cumulonimbus clouds can be seen in the summer sky.

examples.japanese: {入道雲|にゅうどうぐも}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出|で}て→出る：00513_deru⟧きた⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{夕立|ゆうだち}→夕立：05862_yuudachi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{来|く}る→来る：00254_kuru⟧⟦かもしれない→かもしれない：00164_kamoshirenai⟧。
examples.english: Thunderhead clouds are forming, so there might be an evening shower.

examples.japanese: ⟦{山|やま}→山：02168_yama⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{向|む}こう⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{巨大|きょだい}→巨大：02586_kyodai⟧な{入道雲|にゅうどうぐも}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧もくもく⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{立|た}ち{上|のぼ}っていた→立ち上る：10670_tachinoboru⟧。
examples.english: A gigantic cumulonimbus cloud was billowing up beyond the mountains.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
The name {入道雲|にゅうどうぐも} comes from {入道|にゅうどう} (Buddhist monk) + ⟦{雲|くも}→雲：02202_kumo⟧ (cloud). The towering white cloud formation resembles the shaved, bald head of a monk.

SEASONAL REFERENCE:
{入道雲|にゅうどうぐも} is a quintessential summer image in Japan, often depicted in art and anime as a symbol of summer vacation and childhood nostalgia.

WEATHER NOTE:
These clouds often bring sudden afternoon thunderstorms (⟦{夕立|ゆうだち}→夕立：05862_yuudachi⟧) in summer.
